newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium calls in anthropologist after bones found.
newsitem.headline: Belgium calls in anthropologist after bones found.

text.p: Police in the central Belgian city of Mons have called in an anthropologist after the discovery at the weekend of the skeletons of 10 people in woods near the city, Belgian radio said on Monday.

The initial discovery by a group of boys playing in the woods prompted fears the bones could belong to more victims of a still unknown serial killer who earlier this year left bin bags full of severed body parts around the city.
However, initial investigations revealed that the bones -- including the full skeletons of five adults and two children -- were at least 30 years old and possibly dated back to the Middle Ages.
The Mons judge in charge of the case called in the anthropologist to determine the exact date and origin of the bones which are now believed to be from the 17th century.
Belgian newspapers speculated on Monday that the skeletons could have come from a community of plague victims who lived in total isolation near the woods.
